# Chapter 4 — Purview DSPM for AI and Copilot Data Posture

::: {.callout-note}
## In this chapter
Data Security Posture Management for AI reports how AI assistants — chiefly Microsoft 365 Copilot — touch organizational data: what is referenced, what is at risk of oversharing, and which interactions warrant review. The reports are only actionable when their findings can be attributed to organizational position. This chapter binds DSPM for AI to OrgPath so Copilot oversharing risk, sensitive-prompt activity, and AI-interaction auditing are all readable by segment, and so the remediation work the posture surfaces lands on the right organizational owner.
:::

## What DSPM for AI Reports, and Why It Is Org-Blind by Default

Describe the surface: Copilot interaction reports, oversharing assessments, sensitive-info-in-prompts signals. Name the gap — the findings are tenant- or user-level and carry no organizational rollup, so leadership cannot see AI risk *by division* and remediation has no structural owner.

## Joining AI-Posture Findings to OrgPath on Both Planes

The conceptual core: DSPM for AI findings touch a user (who prompted) and a data asset (what was referenced). Both already carry OrgPath — the user from Book 07's user plane, the asset from Book 07a's data plane. Joining findings to OrgPath on both sides produces an AI-risk view indexed by organizational segment.

## Copilot Oversharing as an OrgPath-Scoped Remediation Queue

Make it operational: oversharing findings (over-permissioned sites, labels missing on AI-reachable content) become a remediation queue partitioned by OrgPath, routed to the owning segment, and tracked to closure — rather than an undifferentiated tenant-wide backlog no one owns.

## Sensitive-Prompt and Interaction Auditing by Segment

Connect back to the risk and supervision chapters: AI-interaction auditing is a natural input to Insider Risk and Communication Compliance, and OrgPath scoping lets those solutions consume DSPM-for-AI signals for the right populations without over-collecting across the whole tenant.

## GCC-Moderate Availability and the AI-Governance Boundary

Close with the boundary reality: DSPM for AI feature availability, Copilot footprint, and connector support differ in GCC Moderate. Call out explicitly what can be governed in-boundary today versus what is commercial-only, consistent with Book 07a's boundary-caveats discipline.
